html:
LoFTR (Zhejiang University, CVPR 2021): detector-free matching of two photos of one scene with transformers; semi-dense matches as keypoint pairs (the form COLMAP takes). Outdoor (MegaDepth) and indoor (ScanNet) weights. Apache-2.0 code and weights.

Commercial use: yes.

Details
  • Paper: LoFTR: Detector-Free Local Feature Matching with Transformers, CVPR 2021, 2021-04-01
  • Original code: https://github.com/zju3dv/LoFTR at df7ca80f9173
  • Code licence: Apache-2.0 (permissive); files: LICENSE
  • Weights licence: Apache-2.0
  • Licence evidence: https://github.com/zju3dv/LoFTR/blob/df7ca80f917334b94cfbe32cc2901e09a80e70a8/LICENSE ; https://huggingface.co/kornia/loftr/tree/0fb3b456cf176746709c38fa9cf80695a1c82dac
  • Training data: MegaDepth (Internet photo collections with SfM / MVS depth) (loftr-outdoor: MegaDepth. loftr-indoor: ScanNet (ScanNet terms of use: non-commercial research), README training section.)
  • Options: long_side = 840 (>= 0)
  • Kernel libraries: none (not implemented yet: data-dependent match counts (mutual nearest neighbours above a threshold))
  • Variants: loftr-outdoor, loftr-indoor
  • Outputs: keypoints1, keypoints2, pairs, scores
  • Input size: any H x W >= 32, padded to a multiple of 32
  • Tested up to (portable, fp16, RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB): loftr-outdoor 3000x4000 (1.9 GiB peak allocated, 2.8 reserved); loftr-indoor 3000x4000 (2.0 GiB peak allocated, 2.8 reserved)
  • loftr-outdoor 768x1024, first call: portable + torch.compile 33 s (cold Inductor cache).
  • loftr-outdoor original 768x1024: upstream LoFTR default_cfg, temp_bug_fix False, long side 840
  • loftr-indoor original 768x1024: upstream LoFTR default_cfg, temp_bug_fix True, long side 840
  • loftr-outdoor load / first call: original 0.35 s / 0.242 s, portable 0.24 s / 0.578 s
  • loftr-indoor load / first call: original 1.49 s / 0.693 s, portable 0.32 s / 0.53 s
  • Protocol, first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5

Measured

Dense matchers: 5000 matches per pair sampled from the warp by certainty (upstream's balanced KDE sampling); sparse matchers: all their matches of one call (LightGlue, XFeat: LightGlue's MegaDepth-1500 setting; LoFTR, DeDoDe: their card defaults). OpenCV essential-matrix RANSAC (0.5 px threshold, normalised by the mean focal length); AUC of the larger of the rotation and translation-direction errors. Original = the original code named under Details, same checkpoint and protocol.

Parity

CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 3e-05 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.0025 and p99 <= 0.02 (absolute error of the output keypoints1).

Limitations

  • Sparse output: no dense warp. result.matches() gives the matched points for estimate_pose; every match is its own keypoint pair (pairs is [[0, 0], [1, 1], ...]).
  • One image pair per call internally (batches run pair by pair); the match counts differ per pair.
  • No exportable module: the match counts are data-dependent (torch.compile runs with graph breaks; ONNX / TensorRT export fails).
  • Images are converted to grayscale and matched at long_side (default 840, upstream's MegaDepth test size); the coarse matching holds an (H W / 64)^2 score matrix, so memory grows with the 4th power of the side. The indoor weights were evaluated by upstream at 640 x 480 (ScanNet).
